## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\subset H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated as an ideal by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\). [source-2, lines 1382-1401]
- [proved] Under the recorded integral graded presentation hypotheses and the accepted degreewise certificates, if \(a=1,b=2\), then \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\).

## Strategy
Put \(d=ij\) and
\[
x_0=s_{i^j},\qquad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\qquad
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}.
\]
Since \(a=1,b=2\), the source-stated first generating interval is precisely
\[
\{x_0,x_1,x_2\}.
\]
Thus \(J_v=(x_0,x_1,x_2)\). Since the recorded graded presentation has
\(A_0=\mathbb Z\) and \(A=A_0\oplus A_+\), reduction modulo \(A_+J_v\)
gives a graded surjection
\[
\phi:\mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow Q,
\]
where the summands have degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\), respectively.

The accepted degreewise certificates give
\[
Q_d=\mathbb Z\bar x_0,\qquad
Q_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\bar x_1,\qquad
Q_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
Hence each nonzero homogeneous component of \(\phi\)'s domain maps
isomorphically onto the corresponding component of \(Q\). Therefore
\[
(\ker\phi)_d=(\ker\phi)_{d+1}=(\ker\phi)_{d+2}=0.
\]
As \(\ker\phi\) is graded and the domain has no other homogeneous
components, \(\ker\phi=0\). Thus \(\phi\) is an isomorphism:
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2
\cong\mathbb Z^3.
\]

The requested target is established, conditionally on the recorded presentation hypotheses and the three accepted degreewise certificates. No minimality or broader parent claim is concluded.

## Gaps
- The conclusion depends on the stipulated integral graded presentation and on the accepted degreewise certificates; this argument does not independently reprove them.
